text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Telecom group Tele Danmark is asking 130,000 telephone subscribers in western Denmark to pay 350 crowns each if they want to be connected to modernised exchanges from where they can opt for new and cheaper services from competitors NetCom and Telia. Subscribers unprepared to pay will have to wait more than a year to use NetCom and Telia.

--- A new survey made by Politiken shows that during the past few months 10 of Denmark's 50 largest companies in Denmark have entirely or partly replaced switched from Tele Danmark to other providers and that 74 percent of the companies questioned are considering a change.

--- Computer game producer Scanbox, listed on the Copenhagen Stock exchange, expects to gain more than 15 percent of the expanding computer game and multimedia software market in Scandinavia with new sole agency deals with some of the world's most important producers combined with the production of Scanbox products in Danish.

--- Danish power stations' exports to mainly Norway and Sweden rose from 379 million crowns in the first eight months of 1995 to 1,8 billion crowns in the same period this year creating hope in the industry for lower prices for Danish companies.
